column1: # AQL Language Specification: Argument Usurping (usurp / /u)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# usurp f         → wrap a function so its signature arg order is reversed
# name/u          → same, as a word-suffix modifier (resolves + usurps name)
# name/ur         → usurp combined with ref: leave the wrapper as inert data
# quote (usurp f) → capture the usurped wrapper as inert data
# A usurped fn called `usurped a b c` dispatches the original as `f c b a`.
# Like ref/`/r`, the wrapper is an unquoted Function value: it dispatches
# when args follow (forward / paren-grouped) and stays inert under quote or
# when reffed.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2 10 3
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp (ref sub2) 10 3
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/u 10 3
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (usurp (ref sub2)) 10 3
def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  inc/u 5
column3: usurp of a 1-arg fn is a no-op on order

column1: def cat3 fn [[a:String b:String c:String][String][a add b add c]]  cat3/u 'x' 'y' 'z'
def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f 7 'hi'
def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f/u 'hi' 7
column3: usurped sig is [String Integer]; a=7 b='hi'

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def ops {rev: (usurp (ref sub2))}  ops.rev 10 3
column3: wrapper captured in a map dispatches via dot-access

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  quote (usurp (ref inc))
column3: quoted usurp is inert data — the Function value itself

column1: nope/u
def x 5  x/u
column3: /u on a non-fn binding is rejected

column1: def x 5  usurp x
column3: usurp word rejects a non-function value (Function slot unmatched)
